āchāryān mātulān bhrātṝīn putrān pautrān sakhīṁs tathā
śhvaśhurān suhṛidaśh chaiva senayor ubhayor api
theme: Arjuna Sees Family on Both Sides
hindi: वहाँ, दोनों सेनाओं के बीच खड़े होकर, अर्जुन ने अपने पिता के समान बड़ों, दादाओं, गुरुओं, मामाओं, भाइयों, पुत्रों, पौत्रों और मित्रों को देखा। उसने ससुरों और शुभचिंतकों को भी वहीं खड़ा देखा।
english: There, standing between the two armies, Arjuna saw his elders, grandfathers, teachers, uncles, brothers, sons, grandsons and friends. He also saw his fathers-in-law and well-wishers, standing in both armies.
deeper: Krishna had said, “Look at the Kurus gathered here” (1.25). Arjuna looked, and he did not see enemy soldiers. He saw his own people. Until now the war had been an idea. Now it had faces, names and memories.

Notice the long list: fathers, grandfathers, teachers, uncles, brothers, sons, grandsons, friends. Arjuna is slowly counting everyone he loves who is about to be hurt. The verse shows us a heart that is starting to feel. Some of this feeling is love and some is fear, and it grows in the verses that follow.

The lesson for us is to look closely before we act. When we really see the people affected by a choice, we understand its cost. The Gita will later guide Arjuna to hold both his feelings and his duty with a steady mind. For today, simply noticing is the first step.
words: fathers, elders of the father’s generation
background: The two great armies, the Pandavas and the Kauravas, stood ready on the field of Kurukshetra. Arjuna asked Krishna to place his chariot between them so that he could see who had come to fight (1.21–1.23). Krishna, the Lord of the senses, drew the finest chariot right into the middle (1.24).
Standing in front of Bhishma, Drona and all the kings, Krishna said, “Partha, look at all these Kurus gathered here” (1.25). This verse tells us what Arjuna saw when he looked.
lessons: Really seeing the people our choices affect helps us act more wisely.
Arjuna’s heart began to stir, and it is natural to feel deeply when family is involved.
Behind every side in any quarrel there are people who love and are loved.
Krishna gave Arjuna a quiet moment to look, which is often the first step towards understanding.
Arjuna names his elders and teachers first, showing how much he valued them.
examples: Aarav’s cricket team plays his cousins’ team. When he sees Chinku and Meena in the opposite team, the game suddenly feels different. He realises winning is not the only thing that matters.
In a school debate, Diya has to argue against her favourite teacher’s team. She feels a little shy and confused. It shows how much respect she has for her teacher.
Rohan is angry with his brother over a toy. Then he sees his brother’s teary eyes and his anger starts melting. Looking closely at someone’s face can soften us.
On sports day, Kavya’s best friend is placed in the rival house. Seeing her across the field, Kavya feels both excited and a bit sad. Both feelings are normal.
Before a family argument, Ishaan looks around the table and sees Dadaji, Dadi, Mummy and his little sister. He understands that his words will touch all of them.
Two friends, Sana and Pooja, both stand for class monitor. Standing together on the stage, each realises she is competing with someone she cares about. They promise to stay friends either way.
Manav and his neighbour Tara both want the lead role. When Tara’s name is called, Manav sees how nervous she is. He cheers for her, even while hoping to do his best.
Before replying angrily to a classmate, Neel takes a deep breath and looks at him properly. He notices the boy is upset too. That small pause changes the whole conversation.

story.title: Little Arjuna on Bhishma’s Lap
paras: In the Mahabharata, the Pandava and Kaurava princes grew up together in Hastinapura. The one who watched over them all was Bhishma, their wise and gentle grandfather’s elder, whom everyone respected deeply.
Arjuna later remembered how, as a small boy, he used to run to Bhishma after playing in the dust. He would climb on his lap, covered in dirt, and call him “Father!”
Bhishma would smile and say, “Child, I am not your father. I am your father’s father.” Arjuna never forgot the warmth of that lap and the love in that voice.
Now, on the battlefield, that same Bhishma stood across from him. It is no wonder that when Arjuna looked at the armies, his heart filled with memories, love and worry.
story.moral: Lesson: When we truly look at the people around us, our heart remembers love, and that helps us think carefully before we act.

quiz.q: Whom did Arjuna see standing in the two armies?
o: His elders, teachers, relatives and friends
quiz.x: Arjuna saw fathers, grandfathers, teachers, uncles, brothers, sons, grandsons and friends on both sides.

quiz.q: Who asked Arjuna to look at the Kurus gathered there?
quiz.x: In verse 1.25, Krishna told Arjuna, “Partha, look at all these Kurus gathered here.”

quiz.q: What does the name “Partha” mean here?
quiz.x: Partha means the son of Pritha (Kunti), a loving name for Arjuna.

quiz.q: What is a good lesson from this verse?
o: Look closely and notice who our actions affect
quiz.x: Seeing people clearly helps us understand the real cost of our choices.

reel.hook: What happens when you look closely at the people you’re fighting?
reel.lesson: Look closely at the people your actions touch before you decide.
reel.caption:
Arjuna looked across the battlefield and saw his own family. 💛
Before the next argument, pause and really look at the person in front of you.
Gita verse 1.26, a small step towards a wiser heart. 🙏
